title: Restrict all Codex normative content to principles only
summary: Codex records principles only;implementation and business rules remain owner-local outside legal content;preserve safety and authority boundaries while legacy detailed-content migration remains incomplete.
origin: direct human-governor instruction: Codex records principles only;implementation rules and business rules do not enter the Codex;law/data only,no runtime implementation

changes.proposed: SCOPE:the Codex records principles only,including legitimate authority,ownership boundaries,separation of duties,permission,data custody,isolation,safety,accountability,evidence,independent verification,interpretation and governed change. EXCLUSION:implementation rules and business rules do not enter the Codex;algorithms,programming languages,software stacks,files,paths,APIs,schemas,protocol layouts,technical versions,model topology,parameters,thresholds,test-suite composition,scheduling procedures and business decision procedures belong to their governed owners outside the Codex. APPLICABILITY:this boundary controls every general provision,special law,ordinance and purported normative registry payload;registration,format or writing style cannot turn an excluded detail into a legal principle. EXTERNAL-OWNERSHIP:owner-local contracts,policies,configuration and business specifications may have bounded operational authority,but never independent Codex authority or power to enlarge permissions. REFERENCES:the Codex may identify the responsible owner and controlling principle without importing the external rule payload or making an implementation choice a legal mandate. LEGACY:excluded details remaining in existing records are non-operative legacy material for lawful owner-local migration,not current Codex authority;principles contained in a mixed record remain binding. MIGRATION:migration requires attributable ownership,evidence and independent validation;unresolved custody or equivalence remains incomplete and cannot be declared complete by relabeling. SAFETY:separating principles from implementation does not waive current permissions,approved safety controls,independent verification or release gates;uncertain authority fails closed. AUTHORITY:only the governed current principle record is legal authority;translations,mirrors,implementation projections and audit measurements create no additional law.

CONTENT:B5 principles-only scope applies before representation or classification. REPRESENTATION:a canonical provision identifies the principle,its scope,responsible authority,legal effect and governed lineage;human-readable or structured wording does not change the principle's authority. NARRATIVE:registered wording of a principle may state its legal duty;commentary,examples,translations and legacy implementation or business descriptions create no independent duty. MACHINE-PROJECTION:evaluators,executable predicates,schemas,field definitions and checker algorithms are nonlaw implementation artifacts maintained by their owners outside the Codex;they may verify adherence to a principle but cannot author,replace or broaden it. PARITY:verification requires independently attributable evidence that the external mechanism faithfully implements the controlling principle;registration,format,labels or matching text alone do not prove conformance. GAP:an unresolved implementation,classification or migration gap remains incomplete and does not invalidate the controlling principle or authorize a bypass. CHANGE:semantic amendments require governed successor authority and preserved lineage;mechanical style rewriting must not silently change meaning or identity.

CLASSIFICATION:each current provision has one declared primary normative class;classification applies only to principles eligible under B5. EXPLANATORY creates no independent duty;HISTORICAL preserves non-operative lineage;NORMATIVE_MANUAL is a principle requiring accountable review;MACHINE_ENFORCED is a principle whose external enforcement requires independently verified conformance;RELEASE_BLOCKING is a principle whose unresolved verification denies affected release;SUPERSEDED resolves to its controlling current successor. SECONDARY-TAGS:enforcement and release effects do not create new law or override the content boundary. EXCLUSION:implementation and business content cannot become normative through classification,registration,an evaluator or a matching digest. OWNERSHIP:mechanism specifications,business procedures,executable predicates and concrete evidence formats remain owner-local outside the Codex;only the controlling principle and accountability relation belong in law. DEFAULT:missing classification or evidence remains incomplete and never silently grants machine authority or release approval. MIXED-RECORD:retain the governing principle,exclude implementation and business portions from current legal effect,and track their owner-local migration without claiming completed removal. CONFORMANCE:an external mechanism must resolve to one controlling principle and independent current evidence;it cannot alter the principle or substitute its own acceptance rule.

CONTROL:B162 defines the current five-core responsibility boundary;B5 excludes implementation and business rules from this provision and all other law. DECISION-CORE:owns governed decisions and result acceptance within its granted general scope,without direct execution. PERMISSION-CORE:owns identity,permission and governance-directory accountability,without business execution or Codex content self-authorization. RUNTIME-CORE:owns authorized execution and lifecycle control,without permission generation,self-authorization or policy alteration. AUTOMATION-CORE:owns bounded orchestration and coordination,without execution authority,permission generation or result acceptance. XINGCHENG-ASSISTANT:owns independent inspection,audit and notification,without substituting user choice or acquiring Xingcheng data,repair,upgrade or learning authority. XINGCHENG:is a separate institution with independent identity,lifecycle and exclusive owner-held data;its bounded special-law powers remain governed by B81 and do not transfer to a tool or assistant. SUB-SOVEREIGNS:abolished and historical only. EXECUTION-BOUNDARY:authorized work is attributable to a registered owner and accountable executor;isolation containers create no business authority and modules cannot self-authorize or acquire another owner's power. OWNERSHIP:one current owner and one primary responsibility govern each capability;coordination or delegation does not expand scope. EXTERNAL-RULES:language choices,technical contracts,algorithms,parameters,business decisions and operational tuning are governed outside the Codex by the responsible owner under current permission,safety,evidence and independent-verification principles;their operational authority is not legal authority. LEGACY:implementation-specific wording in this or another provision is non-operative Codex detail under B5 and remains an explicit migration gap until lawful external custody and equivalence are validated.
